blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Lamport's 'Paxos made simple' as a clear and accessible explanation of the Paxos consensus algorithm, which was previously considered difficult to understand due to its allegorical original presentation. The blog emphasizes that the core of the algorithm is surprisingly simple, relying on the fundamental property of majorities: if a majority of nodes agree on a value, no other majority can agree on a different value. Colyer breaks down the paper's structure, explaining the three roles (proposer, acceptor, learner) and the two-phase protocol (Prepare and Accept phases) that ensures consensus. He notes the paper's step-by-step derivation of the protocol and its practical implications for building fault-tolerant distributed systems, including the concept of multi-Paxos for implementing a distributed state machine.
paper_abstract: The Paxos algorithm, when presented in plain English, is very simple. Contents
